measurements.name: completed
measurements.sql: SELECT max(completed_at) AS t FROM checks WHERE lifecycle IN('COMPLETED','CANCELLED','ABANDONED')

measurements.name: queued
measurements.sql: SELECT max(queued_at) AS t FROM checks WHERE lifecycle='QUEUED'

plan.detail: SEARCH checks USING COVERING INDEX checks_queued

measurements.name: started
measurements.sql: SELECT max((SELECT max(started_at) FROM checks WHERE monitor_id=monitors.id)) AS t FROM monitors

plan.detail: SEARCH monitors USING COVERING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_monitors_1
SEARCH checks USING COVERING INDEX checks_monitor_started (monitor_id=?)

measurements.name: recovery
measurements.sql: UPDATE checks SET lifecycle='ABANDONED',terminal_order=(SELECT value FROM check_commit_clock WHERE id=1),completed_at=1,outcome=NULL,http_status=NULL,duration_ms=NULL,error_code=NULL WHERE lifecycle IN('QUEUED','RUNNING')

plan.detail: SEARCH check_commit_clock USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid=?)

rationale: After full integrity and foreign-key validation, terminal completion bounds queued/started clocks, RUNNING requires a started clock, and QUEUED is probed independently. Each monitor uses the existing covering started-time index. These exact maxima preserve nullable and unfinished execution recovery without scanning retained checks.
limitation: Component measurements only; application startup still includes mandatory full writable quick_check and foreign_key_check. No ten-second startup pass is claimed.
